cues.en: You can judge for yourself.

cues.en: And I found that if you just say the correct stuff

cues.en: Yep, pretty much covers it.

cues.en: more confident in the things they thought beforehand.

cues.en: So what you're saying is you make people look stupid so you can teach others -- how noble!

cues.en: There's a difference between being unknowledgeable and being unintelligent.

cues.en: I mean I'm unknowledgeable about lots of stuff.

cues.zh: 科学确实很难——尤其是因为很多概念都是反直觉的。
cues.en: And science can be hard -- for the particular reason that it's counterintuitive.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得我们应该先承认大家是怎么想的，大部分人是怎么理解的，
cues.en: So I think we should acknowledge what everyone is thinking, what most people are thinking

cues.en: and use that as our basis for teaching.

cues.en: But if you actually believe that, then why does your face light up with glee every time

cues.en: you hear a misconception?

cues.zh: 我能帮助大家了解真相——这也是 Veritasium 的初衷——
cues.en: I can help people learn the truth -- and that's the point of Veritasium -- to help people

cues.zh: 帮助人们理解自然界的真理，并在自己的生活中探寻真理。
cues.en: understand the truths of the natural world and seek the truth in their own lives.

cues.en: As Richard Feynman said, "The first principle is that you must not fool yourself -- and

cues.en: you are the easiest person to fool."
